label: Открытый / Закрытый
description: Открытый vs закрытый: open/closed contrasts across genders and everyday scenes.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine nominative agreement. 'Открытый', a participle-adjective from 'открыть', takes the masculine ending to match 'магазин'. The everyday remark anchors the form in daily errands.

Strategic focus: Feminine nominative agreement. 'Закрытая', a participle-adjective from 'закрыть', takes the feminine ending to match 'дверь'. The sentence roots the form in a familiar household scene.
Strategic focus: Neuter nominative agreement. 'Открытое' takes the neuter ending to match 'окно'. The image of fresh air makes the neuter participle-adjective concrete.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Закрытые' takes the plural ending to match 'окна'. The everyday detail fixes the plural participle-adjective in mind.

missions.phrase: Открытый банк работает, а закрытый отдыхает.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Direct masculine contrast. Both 'открытый' and 'закрытый' are nominative for the masculine 'банк'. The sentence pairs the open and closed participle-adjectives in one comparison.
Strategic focus: Feminine accusative agreement. 'Открытую' matches the feminine 'дверь' as the object of 'закрой'. The short command keeps the participle-adjective practical.
Strategic focus: Feminine instrumental in the predicate. After past-tense 'была', 'закрытой' takes the feminine instrumental ending to match 'касса'. This shows the быть-plus-instrumental pattern.
Strategic focus: Plural instrumental in the predicate. After 'были', 'открытыми' takes the plural instrumental ending to match 'двери'. The sentence extends the pattern into the plural.
Strategic focus: Short-form masculine predicate. The short form 'открыт' states a present state of 'вход' without an ending. Short forms are typical for these participle-adjectives in the predicate.

Strategic focus: Short-form masculine predicate. The short form 'закрыт' states the current status of 'музей'. The schedule note shows how naturally the short participle-adjective works in everyday speech.
